findings.description: The bucket has no acl set (defaults may be overridden by comments indicating public access) and no bucket_public_access_block configured, allowing potential public read/write access to sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket, including the customer master file, are stored unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, which combined with force_destroy=true and public exposure increases risk of irreversible data loss or tampering of sensitive customer data.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in public unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A sensitive customer master spreadsheet is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is publicly accessible and unencrypted, directly exposing PII/financial customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled for the financials bucket, combined with force_destroy=true, risking permanent loss or undetected tampering of financial records.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving data science datasets unencrypted at rest.
